summary: A 1922 stone-cabin site with a 1956 L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete base; staffed in the fire season and on the National Historic Lookout Register since 2020.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete base (current cab, 1956); site used for a lookout since 1922
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest

events.note: First lookout on the site: a 12x12 stone cabin with a metal roof
January 1945 newspaper item says the Pine district used four women as lookouts, one on Trinity Mountain
December 1955 ground party organized in Boise to reach men who had been in a crash in snow-covered terrain; they apparently spent the night in the lookout station
L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete base replaced the stone cabin (NHLR, Rex's page and Forest Lookouts give 1956 as the build date)

corrections.why: Sources give a 10-foot (about 3 m) concrete base under the cab. The base height is not the total height of the tower, and no source gives the total.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Fire Lookouts (1922 current structure) and Keeping Watch (Built: 1922) disagree with NHLR, Rex's page and Forest Lookouts, which date the L-4 cab to 1956. The 1922 date belongs to the first stone cabin and the site. The record uses 1922 for the first cabin and 1956 for the cab.
NHLR gives 9,434 ft (2,875 m) and Rex's Fire Lookout Page gives 9,451 ft. The record keeps the NHLR value; the story reports the range.

notes_for_editor: Staffing is dated: Idaho Fire Lookouts gives a page date of September 3, 2021 and a staff list running to approximate 2008 to 2023, so current staffing may differ. Access level is not stated on any page read; the story asks visitors to get permission first. The brief's height_m 3.0 is the 10-foot base only and is proposed for removal. The 1922 vs 1956 build-year conflict is recorded in resolved_conflicts.
